blocks.text: Verse 1 attributes David’s decision to count Israel to Satan (or an adversary). A parallel account in 2 Samuel begins instead with the LORD’s anger. Readers have offered harmonizing, developmental, and distinct-source explanations for this difference, but the relationship between the two accounts remains debated.

The chapter’s closing scene does more than bring the plague to an end. After David builds an altar on Ornan’s threshing floor, this location is identified as the site for the LORD’s house and altar. The purchase and sacrifice in verses 18–30 therefore give the place lasting importance within the account.
